channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Deadly Russian Attacks On Ukraine Hit Medical Center, Science Academy
item.description: Russian forces struck civilian sites on 28 September, setting fire to the National Academy of Sciences and a major medical clinic in Kyiv. An office building in Dnipro and an apartment block in Kharkiv also suffered damage. The attacks caused casualties and disrupted services. A wave of Russian attacks hit civilian sites in several Ukrainian cities on September 28. In Kyiv, fire broke out after strikes on the National Academy of Sciences and a major medical clinic.

item.title: Why Israel banned Arab parties ahead of polls
item.description: Recent polls by media outlets have suggested that neither Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition nor the Zionist opposition bloc will be able to secure 61 seats required for parliamentary majority in the 120-member Knesset and projected that the Arab parties could win up to 12 seats Why Israel banned Arab parties ahead of polls.

item.title: Iran supreme leader says U.S. will be forced out of West Asia: state TV
item.description: ‘Today, having suffered painful blows at the hands of valiant fighters and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, they [the enemies] do not venture beyond the Arabian Sea,’ Mojtaba Khamenei said in the written statement attributed to him Iran supreme leader says U. S. will be forced out of West Asia: state TV. Iran supreme leader says U. S.

item.title: Kallas Says Russia's Mockery Of UN Meeting Shows It's Not Interested In Ending Ukraine War
item.description: European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on September 28 that Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's treatment of his German counterpart, Johann Wadephul, after their recent UN meeting demonstrates that Russia is not interested in peace in Ukraine. Kallas Says Russia's Mockery Of UN Meeting Shows It's Not Interested In Ending Ukraine War.

item.title: Refugee funding, US migration policy triggers ‘cascade’ of rights violations, world forests report
item.description: Support for water and sanitation at the biggest camp in the world for Syrian refugees is under threat from a lack of funding – combined with the impact of climate change – the UN Children’s Fund, UNICEF, said on Monday. Refugee funding, US migration policy triggers ‘cascade’ of rights violations, world forests report.

item.title: Ambassadors meet as West Bank tensions rise, Gaza plan stalls
item.description: The Security Council met Monday morning with prospects for peace in the Middle East under strain on two fronts. In the West Bank, settler violence and settlement expansion are raising fears for a two-State solution. In Gaza, a year-old peace plan has stalled while civilian suffering continues.

item.title: World leaders take stock of global fight against racism
item.description: World leaders are meeting in the General Assembly to assess how far the world has come in combating racism and how far it still has to go. The Durban Declaration and Programme of Action, the most comprehensive framework of its kind, seeks to acknowledge historical injustices, dismantle inequalities and build societies grounded in dignity, equality and justice for all. World leaders take stock of global fight against racism.

item.title: DR Congo Ebola emergency: Calls grow for urgent humanitarian access
item.description: Aid teams trying to keep deadly Ebola disease from spreading in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are increasingly concerned about ongoing fighting and violence that has forced thousands of people to flee a displacement camp in the vast, resource-rich east of the country. DR Congo Ebola emergency: Calls grow for urgent humanitarian access.

item.title: Erdogan playing East and West, winning room to maneuver
item.description: Less than two months after his government hosted the NATO summit. which was framed as proof of Turkey’s pivotal role in transatlantic security. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has proposed full Turkish membership in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, an entity that has been described as being anti-NATO or a “rogue NATO. Erdogan playing East and West, winning room to maneuver.

item.title: Bangkok declared a ‘disaster zone’ after flooding, as rainstorms shift direction
item.description: Capital city submerged in waist-high flood water, while elsewhere Hurricane Nolo threatens Hawaii’s Big IslandBangkok was declared a disaster zone by its city officials towards the end of last week, after streets in Thailand’s capital city were submerged in up to waist-high flood water. The flooding stemmed from an active cell of low pressure across central Thailand that brought continuous heavy r.

item.title: Trump family-tied drone maker woos Pakistan at India’s expense
item.description: Powerus, a US defense company with ties to President Donald Trump’s sons, drew scrutiny after signing a memorandum of understanding this month with the Pakistani Army and offering Islamabad access to Ukrainian drone technology, sparking debate over the deal’s potential impact on India and wider regional security. Powerus was founded in October 2025 by veterans [] The post Trump family-tied drone.

item.title: Hurricane Nolo still threatens Hawaii as Mexico’s Baja braces for Hurricane Polo
item.description: Hurricane Nolo is moving away from Hawaiian islands but threat of heavy rain, flash floods and strong winds persistsHurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms. Hurricane Nolo still threatens Hawaii as Mexico's Baja braces for major Hurricane Polo.

item.title: Trump rejects deal, Iran diplomat calls for ‘negotiated solution’
item.description: As US President Donald Trump publicly rejected Iran’s proposal for a ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz this weekend, the Iranian foreign minister reiterated that “there is no alternative to a negotiated solution.” “There’s always hope for diplomacy,” though the Trump-led United States has been an untrustworthy negotiator, Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said during a Sunday appear Trump rejects deal, Iran diplomat calls for ‘negotiated solution’.

item.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to
item.description: Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answerCape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents. The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activis.

item.title: US challenges China on secret nuclear tests as arms race looms
item.description: A mounting standoff over allegations of covert Chinese nuclear testing and rapid arsenal expansion has collided with an intensifying domestic debate within the US over whether it must abandon its decades-long test moratorium. US officials are pressing China in confidential diplomatic talks over suspected low-yield nuclear testing and a rapid strategic expansion across at least [] The post US chal.

item.title: US strikes on Ecuadorian fishing boats raise humanitarian concerns but Trump admin not wavering
item.description: Attorney says fishers ‘losing their livelihoods’, but Marco Rubio maintains US still willing to ‘blow up ships if need be’While the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, was being decorated in Quito by Ecuador’s president for “helping to promote peace in the region”, 10 Ecuadorian fishers whose boat had been blown up by US forces were adrift in the eastern Pacific.

item.title: Canada urges stronger partnerships as global order faces ‘rupture’
item.description: Canada’s Foreign Minister Anita Anand warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that the international order has entered an era of profound disruption, calling for stronger multilateral cooperation and new partnerships as major powers increasingly turn away from global economic integration. Canada urges stronger partnerships as global order faces ‘rupture’.

item.title: Saudi Arabia warns Gulf security inseparable from global stability amid regional tensions
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister warned on Saturday that escalating threats across the Middle East risked international peace, energy security and global trade, calling for stronger international cooperation to protect Gulf States and vital shipping routes. Saudi Arabia warns Gulf security inseparable from global stability amid regional tensions.

item.title: Cuba warns against ‘law of the jungle’ as Foreign Minister denounces US pressure
item.description: Cuba’s Foreign Minister warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that escalating military and economic pressure in Latin America and the Caribbean was threatening international law, while accusing the United States of intensifying a decades-long campaign to isolate and weaken his country. Cuba warns against ‘law of the jungle’ as Foreign Minister denounces US pressure.

item.title: Lavrov issues call for new Eurasian ‘security architecture’
item.description: Russia's Foreign Minister, Sergey Lavrov, accused Western countries of destabilising the world through “force and double standards” in his address to the UN General Assembly on Saturday, vowing that Moscow's “special military operation” in Ukraine would be “carried through to the end.” Lavrov issues call for new Eurasian ‘security architecture’.
